sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 131.3 ± 37.9 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunofluorescence on live non-permeabilized HEK293T cells: OR4B1 scored positive for surface expression (tag detected at the plasma membrane). No ligand-binding or downstream signalling assay reported in these clips.
sites.rationale: OR4B1 is a GPCR with no signal peptide (topology string begins with O at residue 1); the N-terminus (residues 1–23) is extracellular and is the sole extracellular terminus — the C-terminus (residues 288–309) is intracellular. Both ledger lines describe N-terminal epitope tags on the full-length receptor; no residue number is stated, but with exactly one extracellular terminus the junction is unambiguous: insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before M1). Computed: residue_after = seq[0] = M; 23 aa of extracellular space separates the prepend position from TM1 (residue 24), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. L2 directly validates surface accessibility of the tag by live-cell Flag immunofluorescence. L1 (PMC9022881) reports OR4B1 cloned as a full-length receptor in pME18S with N-terminal FLAG and 20-aa bovine rhodopsin epitope tags for heterologous expression. L2 (PMC3698168) confirms surface display of Flag-tagged OR4B1 by live-cell, non-permeabilized immunofluorescence with a Flag antibody, establishing that the N-terminal tag is accessible on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: Live, non-permeabilized HEK 293T cells were surface labeled with a Flag antibody to detect membrane associated receptor and OR surface expression was scored based on detectable surface immunofluorescence.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available (L1, L2); both describe the same N-terminal FLAG/Rho tag construct on full-length OR4B1 and together support a single site. No ledger line mentions any internal extracellular loop (ECL1 81–95, ECL2 163–191, ECL3 256–267) or any other junction, so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminus (residues 288–309) is intracellular and cannot carry a surface tag. No signal peptide is present, so the prepended tag will not be cleaved. The cited tag in L1 is actually a dual tag (FLAG + 20-aa Rho N-terminal sequence); both are N-terminal prepends and map to the same junction.
